articles.title: Parents whose sons died from kratom use offer warnings as the drug remains legal
articles.summary: Kratom, a substance that acts on opioid receptors, can be as easy to obtain as a bag of chips. Kratom is derived from a tree native to Southeast Asia, where for generations people have chewed the leaves or boiled them to make a stimulating tea with opioid effects. The sales of kratom in the U.S. have fueled a billion-dollar industry, with products containing the plant available online and in tens of thousands of stores across the country, including gas stations. The kratom industry hails the substance as a mild stimulant that can also aid in recovery from opioid addiction. The kratom industry has supporters in the highest ranks of government and is legally sold in most states. But health experts warn that kratom use can lead to addiction and death. Dr. Andrew Kolodny, the medical director for the Opioid Policy Research Collaborative at Brandeis University, said that it has effects very similar to those of oxycodone, heroin and even fentanyl. The Centers for Disease Control and Prevention has detected kratom in more than 5,000 overdose deaths from 2020-2024. Helping shape perception of kratom as a benign health supplement is the consumer advocacy and lobby group the American Kratom Association. The group describes natural kratom as "a safe food used by many as an herbal supplement" taken for "health and wellbeing or for an energy boost." Four families told "60 Minutes" that their sons, all recently deceased, started using kratom for those kinds of benefits. Susan Eppard's son Matthew told her it was like coffee, because he read it was related to the coffee family. Patti Wheeler's son Wyatt said it was helping him ease away from alcohol. "He was looking for something for energy. A friend of his told him it was safer than Red Bull," said Wendy Chamberlain about her son Joe. The deaths of Matthew and Joe were attributed solely to mitragynine, the main opioid in kratom. Daniel Bregger and Wyatt Wheeler's causes of death included mitragynine along with prescription or over-the-counter medications. Susan Eppard said her son collapsed suddenly while playing cards with friends. She recalled the day her son died. "They tried resuscitating him for a long time. [By the] time I got there, they wouldn't let me in at first, so I'd just sit out on the ground outside screaming for God to keep my baby here," Susan Eppard said. "And they finally let me go in there and see him. I knelt down to him and gave him a kiss on his forehead. And he was just cold and dark and gray." Justin Brower, a toxicologist at NMS Labs, a forensic testing facility 40 minutes outside Philadelphia, said he has analyzed thousands of deaths involving kratom. "Dozens and dozens" have been attributed "just to kratom, no other drugs at all," he said. Fatalities linked to kratom have "increased probably about tenfold" since 2014, he said. "It's pretty incredible how it's taken hold of the United States and how many people are using it now, compared to, you know, a decade-plus ago," Brower said. The Food and Drug Administration warns "consumers not to use kratom because of the risk of serious adverse events, including liver toxicity, seizures, and substance use disorder." With concern growing over kratom-derived products, including the concentrated kratom-related synthetic substance 7-OH, the federal government announced in July that it would restrict 7-OH and three related substances found in kratom products. But then last month, the Department of Health and Human Services changed its recommendation . Among the new recommendations: increasing the amount of 7-OH allowed in products by 20-fold. Some health officials, including former FDA Commissioner Dr. Marty Makary and former senior HHS advisor Calley Means, were stunned by the decision. "60 Minutes" found public filings from the last decade that show a constant stream of cash -- much from the American Kratom Association — earmarked for lobbying the FDA, HHS, the White House, and members of Congress. Millions of dollars committed to keeping kratom legal. Even more money has come in the form of political contributions and investments. Kolodny compared it to the lobbying actions of Purdue Pharma, the manufacturer of OxyContin. "Some of the same scientists who Purdue Pharma hired to make sure that regulators wouldn't take action against OxyContin are now working for the Kratom Association and delivering the same message, downplaying the risks, exaggerating the numbers of people who are potentially benefiting," Kolodny said. HHS declined an interview request with "60 Minutes," but said in a statement that "Neither political contributions nor outside pressure influenced" the decision to increase the amount of 7-OH allowed in products. The American Kratom Association gave a statement to "60 Minutes" and emphasized the distinction between natural kratom and "dangerous chemically manipulated products." Eppard said she can't believe that kratom, in any form, is still for sale. She said she often goes into convenience stores to ask employees if they realize what they are selling. Often, they don't, she said. So she tells them about her son. "We all just miss him terrible," she told "60 Minutes." articles.title: Trump to fly Qatari-gifted jet to Asia, but issue of whether it's been 'maxed out' is unclear
articles.summary: In recent months, Air Force One has received some “cosmetic” enhancements to the interior, but that did not cover the larger work that the White House said would take place eventually. (Andrew Harnik / Getty Images) President Donald Trump is expected to take the Qatari-gifted Air Force One to Asia on Monday as questions linger about upgrades the White House said were needed after a security threat from Iran forced the president to fly home from Turkey on a secret military plane in July, according to two U.S. officials. For months, Trump has said the jet from the Qataris would be “going away” to get “maxed out” so it could “go into any territory.” In September, he said those changes to the plane would “take about 60 days.” The president flew on the new Air Force One to Ireland that month without any issues. He then used the plane regularly during a midterm travel blitz in October, which meant it was not out of commission for an extended period. Instead, the plane has received some improvements and periodic maintenance, but it is unclear whether it has been fully “maxed out,” per the officials. A longer upgrade period is expected in the future, according to one of the officials, but those upgrades will not take a full 60 days. In recent months, the plane has received some “cosmetic” enhancements to the interior, the other U.S. official said, but that did not cover the larger work that the White House said would take place eventually. “We don’t comment on specific upgrades or modifications to Air Force Once,” a senior administration official told NBC News in a statement. “We maintain a consistent posture that ensures a safe, secure, and reliable capability for the President of the United States and routinely evolve the capability as required to maintain that posture. It is the greatest Presidential plane ever built.” In July, Trump said the plane “has a lot of capability.” “But as I understand it, in about a month ​or so, they’re gonna send it to have it be maxed out,” he said. “It’ll take about a month.” Trump did not detail the nature of the work, and the White House has not explained why the original assessment of 30 days later doubled to 60 days. At the time, then-White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt said in a statement that the new Air Force One was “perfectly safe” for domestic and overseas travel but noted in July that the plane would “receive additional upgrades and enhancements in the fall which will take approximately one month to complete.” This article was originally published on NBCNews.com This article originally appeared on NBC News at https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/trump-administration/trump-plans-take-qatari-jet-asia-s-unclear-whether-s-maxed-rcna609487

articles.title: Founder of notorious Guadalajara cartel, imprisoned since 1989, dies at 80
articles.summary: By Diego Oré and Michelle Freyria MEXICO CITY/GUADALAJARA, Nov 15 (Reuters) - Miguel Angel Felix Gallardo, founder of one of Mexico's first major drug cartels whose conviction for the 1985 killing of a US drug-enforcement ‌agent made him one of the country's most notorious traffickers, died in hospital on Sunday at age 80. Local ‌security authorities said Felix Gallardo was transferred to a private hospital in the western city of Guadalajara two days ago but suffered multiple organ ​failure and died around 2 p.m. on Sunday. Imprisoned since 1989, Felix Gallardo was an inmate in a maximum-security prison in western Jalisco state, though his lawyers repeatedly sought house arrest on the grounds of his deteriorating health. Rising to prominence in the 1970s, the former cartel kingpin was an architect of Mexico's modern drug-trafficking trade, igniting a series of turf wars that have led ‌to hundreds of thousands of deaths and ⁠disappearances in ensuing decades. Born in 1946 in Culiacan, Sinaloa, a northwestern state that would later become synonymous with narco-trafficking, he worked as a police officer and bodyguard for a local governor ⁠then became a powerful criminal capo known as the "boss of bosses." Felix Gallardo and others set up the cartel in Guadalajara, the Jalisco state capital and a fast-growing economic powerhouse, becoming the first to move cocaine to the US on a massive scale and ​to forge ​an alliance with Colombian drug barons, including Pablo Escobar's Medellin ​cartel. His narcotics empire expanded in the 1970s and ‌1980s thanks to bribes that won protection from corrupt officials and innovations like using light aircraft to move drugs across the continent, supported by fellow kingpins like Rafael Caro Quintero. His legal battles stretched across decades. Arrested in 1989, Felix Gallardo was sentenced to 40 years in prison on drug-trafficking and weapons charges tied to the Guadalajara cartel. While already incarcerated, he faced a separate prosecution over the 1985 kidnapping and murder of US Drug Enforcement Administration agent Enrique "Kiki" Camarena and Mexican pilot ‌Alfredo Zavala Avelar. Camarena's killing caused a diplomatic dispute with Washington, which pressed ​Mexico hard to arrest those involved. In 2017, a federal court found Felix ​Gallardo guilty in that case and imposed a ​further 37-year sentence. He denied responsibility for the killings. His rise and fall was portrayed on screen ‌by Mexican actor Diego Luna in the 2018 ​hit Netflix series "Narcos: Mexico". Felix Gallardo ​suffered poor health in his final years, and was blind in one eye, practically deaf and unable to walk on his own by the time Spanish-language US network Telemundo interviewed him in prison in 2021. He maintained ​his innocence. "Thirty-two years have passed... That's ‌an eternity for a man who did not commit any crime," he said. (Reporting by Jose Gonzalez in ​Ciudad Juarez and Diego Ore, Noe Torres and Sarah Morland in Mexico City; Additional reporting by Raul ​Cortes; Editing by Rosalba O'Brien, Edmund Klamann and Cynthia Osterman) This article originally appeared on Reuters at https://www.yahoo.com/news/world/articles/mexicos-guadalajara-cartel-founder-aged-213009881.html

articles.title: U.S. colleges struggle as international students turn away
articles.summary: The U.S. has long been a prime landing spot for international students. Thanks to President Donald Trump's visa crackdown, they’re now taking their talents and tuition dollars elsewhere. Tighter visa restrictions, stricter vetting and visa interview and appointment bottlenecks are contributing to what early data suggests will be a steep decline in international student enrollment nationwide this fall. And that was before Trump elevated Stephen Miller — the architect of his immigration agenda and campaign against academia — to chief of staff. The limits on foreign students advances two administration aims: narrowing avenues of potential immigration and hitting the bank accounts of academic institutions conservatives have long criticized. Now, the policy changes, coupled with the administration’s “America First” rhetoric and immigration sweeps, are taking hold, higher education leaders say. “This is great for the United States that they're spending money here, that they're learning about our culture and our country,” Michael Roth, president of Wesleyan University, a private liberal arts school, said of international students. “To just make it harder in the name of some kind of nationalism, it seems like we're shooting ourselves in the foot just to see how good our boots are.” The nationwide enrollment stats for the last academic year are expected to be released this month, but figures released by individual universities signify what is likely to be another slump this fall. The number of international students enrolled at the University of Washington’s Seattle campus declined for a second year in a row , falling to its lowest level in at least a decade. At the Ohio State University, those numbers fell by nearly 13% — the fewest it’s seen in 16 years . And the Illinois Institute of Technology plans to borrow up to $200 million from its endowment because of its declining international student enrollment. Benjamin Johnson, a spokesperson for Ohio State, said in a statement the university’s international student enrollment “strengthens the academic experience” for all of their students. “We want the world’s best and brightest to choose Ohio State for school and stay to build a life and career in Ohio,” Johnson said. Stan Veuger, an economist at the American Enterprise Institute, a conservative-leaning think tank, said the Trump administration’s goal is to “cut off all forms of migration to the maximum extent they can.” And with Miller now serving as the president’s top adviser, “I think it will gradually get worse unless some of the Democrats manage to effectively push back,” he said, referencing the pending Democratic takeover of Congress. Higher education leaders warn that the administration’s ever-changing visa rules and proposed restrictions could permanently damage the country’s appeal to international talent and upend universities’ finances. International students, who often pay full tuition, are an important source of revenue for colleges and sometimes subsidize financial aid and other services for domestic students. “The latest data we have shows that when it comes to bachelor's degree programs at public universities, every international student opens up two spots for American students,” said Zuzana C. Wootson, deputy director of federal policy at the Presidents’ Alliance , which represents 500 presidents and chancellors of public and private colleges and universities. “At the end of the day, who's going to be feeling the harm the most will be domestic students and Americans,” she added. House Education and Workforce Chair Tim Walberg argued the administration’s policies ultimately benefit domestic students. “For the present time, they're helping make sure that the schools are there for who they're supposed to be for,” he said. “When we ultimately find out that we are woefully absent with people in the seats and there are plenty of places available for American students that meet the qualifications, then I think we can start to look at the international.” At Denison University in Ohio, President Adam Weinberg said his school is getting questions from concerned parents of foreign students because of all the policy changes. He said it’s too early to tell what their foreign enrollment will look like, but “we expect pretty steep declines.” International students make up 17% of the private liberal arts school’s student body . “I am absolutely in favor of immigration control and making sure that we're following our laws,” Weinberg said. “And we absolutely need to educate U.S. students … colleges and universities should be educating them and preparing them to drive the economy forward. But we're also going to need to attract talent from around the world and we need to keep it.” The Trump administration’s immigration policies and its enforcement mechanisms have “spread a great deal of fear and a great deal of anxiety” among international students, faculty on visas and undocumented students, said Patricia McGuire, president of Trinity Washington University, where international students make less than 2 percent of its enrollment. McGuire said one of her international students was assaulted near a D.C. metro station and didn’t call for help because “she was afraid if she called the police that she would be arrested and deported.” “That is just disgraceful for this country,” she said. Department of Homeland Security and top administration officials, including Vice President JD Vance, last month argued the stricter policies are designed to discourage visa fraud and that Americans should not have to compete against international students for work. "The performative outrage is incredible," an unnamed DHS spokesperson said in a statement. "Where was the outrage when foreign nationals were abusing the system, violating the terms of their student visas, and making a mockery of our immigration laws? If the media really cared about legitimate international students, they would be thanking President Trump for cracking down on the rampant fraud to ensure only those truly intending to study in the United States are given the privilege.” A State Department spokesperson said in a statement that the administration is "protecting our nation and our citizens by upholding the highest standards of national security and public safety through our visa process. As Secretary [Marco] Rubio said, 'a visa is a privilege, not a right.'" The unnamed spokesperson also added that embassies and consulates are prioritizing "thoroughly vetting each visa case above all else," and the agency is encouraging international students to apply for their visa "as early as they can" in anticipation of "additional processing time for these visa categories." "The United States continues to welcome qualified international students whose academic pursuits contribute to American colleges and universities, support the U.S. economy, and strengthen our nation's global competitiveness," the spokesperson said. If foreign student enrollment plummets as expected, international education advocates warn it might not bounce back the way it has from previous downturns because schools in other countries are eager to compete for these students. Fanta Aw, executive director of NAFSA: Association of International Educators, said the visa appointment situation this summer was “even more difficult” for international students than it was during the Covid-19 pandemic, which spurred a 46% decline among those studying at a U.S. university for the first time. “There is a very intentional attempt by this government to close the doors,” Aw said, adding that prospective students “now understand that uncertainty has become the policy of this administration. … As a result, we have seen expression of interest in the U.S. decline significantly, and with students refocusing their energy on other destinations of choice.” Survey data released Thursday by NAFSA and Study Portals, a research consulting group, found that 50% of colleges in continental Europe saw higher undergraduate enrollments among international students and 59% of Asian schools saw higher postgraduate enrollments between August and October. The DHS spokesperson said “NAFSA’s ‘reporting’ is completely misleading and not backed up by any real evidence" and that the Student and Exchange Visitor Program "has not experienced a 10% drop of foreign student enrollment." A significant factor for international students — especially those at the graduate level — when choosing to study in the United States is the ability to earn work experience. But the Trump administration is seeking to make that much harder, arguing that these programs have become a “back door into the American workforce” and are putting American workers at a disadvantage. In addition to the new procedural regime, the administration is creating new pressure on the nation’s foreign student enrollment with a plan announced last month to sharply raise visa fees. The DHS has proposed a stunning $70,000 fee for each student seeking Optional Practical Training, known as OPT, which is a key driver of foreign student enrollment. Participants made up roughly a quarter of all international students in the United States. Under the administration’s proposal, universities would be responsible for paying the fees. A DHS spokesperson last month said the changes will "require foreign students to justify their worth to employers." Higher education advocates say schools will likely pass the costs on to students. The program allows foreign students on F-1 visas to temporarily work in the United States in jobs related to their fields of study after graduation. It often serves as a bridge for those students to transition to other immigration statuses, like the H-1B visa, a temporary, employer-sponsored visa, to continue working in the country. “We couldn't do it. It wouldn't be affordable for us to do that,” said Wesleyan’s Roth, whose international enrollment has held steady. “Maybe there are super-rich schools that could do that. But for a school, even a small liberal arts college, to do that for their international students who are graduating, it's going to be millions of dollars.” The Trump administration has also proposed steep fees of more than $100,000 for certain new H-1B petitions . And, among other regulatory changes, DHS finalized a separate rule in July requiring foreign students to apply for visa extensions if they need more than four years. A federal court blocked the proposal before it could take effect in September. Veuger said additional limits could be ahead. “You can always impose more fees. You can start suspending universities’ ability to issue the documents they need to renew their visas. You can make it even harder to go get appointments,” he said. “As long as there’s people coming in, they can make it harder.” This article originally appeared on Politico at https://www.politico.com/news/2026/11/15/us-colleges-struggle-as-international-students-turn-away-01164048

articles.title: Jensen Huang reportedly weighs comeback as tech execs lobby Nvidia board
articles.summary: Jensen Huang is considering a return as Nvidia ’s chief executive, days after he resigned over reports that he had affairs with a suspected Chinese spy and a subordinate, the Financial Times reported Sunday. Huang has discussed the possibility with confidants, according to the FT, which cited people familiar with the matter. One ally told the paper they were putting together a “war room” of Silicon Valley executives to lobby Nvidia’s board for his return and would try to win support from the White House. The ally said Huang backed the effort. Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have backed a public letter calling on Nvidia’s board to “Bring Jensen Back.” On Friday, Nvidia shareholders Brad Gerstner of Altimeter Capital and Gavin Baker of Atreides Management urged the board in an open letter to keep “all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang.” A spokesperson for Nvidia and a spokesperson for Huang declined to comment to the FT. Huang doesn’t hold a controlling stake in Nvidia and can’t overrule its board. The push runs into opposition from Washington. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent on Sunday called for a “dramatic shakeup” at Nvidia and urged its board to look outside the company for a new CEO. “I want to keep coming back to what was the culture at Nvidia, and were they pressing these seemingly illicit sales to goose their revenues and their earnings?” Bessent said on Fox News, CNBC reported . He said he wants “answers in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel,” according to Axios . “If this were a bank and they hadn’t complied like this, the OCC would be in there right now, and a lot of the executives would be removed,” Bessent said. Nvidia has said it complies with U.S. export laws. Bessent has also blamed the Commerce Department, led by Secretary Howard Lutnick, for not restricting Megaspeed, the Singapore-based firm at the center of the scandal. “Treasury, War, USTR and State, they were in favor of putting Megaspeed on the Entity List for months, but Commerce has the pen,” Bessent told CNBC on Friday. Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10, CBS News reported . Nvidia reports quarterly earnings Tuesday, its first since Huang’s resignation. Interim CEO Colette Kress has scheduled a company-wide meeting for Wednesday, CNBC reported . The board said Friday it has not yet hired a search firm or “formally engaged any potential candidates” to replace Huang, according to CNBC . The FT reported Friday that the board had approached Arm CEO Rene Haas. Huang resigned Thursday after revelations that he had extramarital affairs with multiple women, one of whom was an alleged Chinese spy. The company said in a statement that Kress, Nvidia’s executive vice president and chief financial officer, will serve as interim CEO. Harvey C. Jones was appointed chair of the board. Nvidia’s stock plunged 13% at the market open Thursday. The company has lost more than $1.2 trillion in market value since the scandal broke in late October, Axios reported. In its statement, the board thanked Huang for his “immeasurable contributions to the company.” The chipmaker is at the center of the global AI economy and has multiple agreements with the U.S. government. Huang, who founded Nvidia in 1993, led the company through the AI boom that made it one of the world’s most valuable publicly traded companies. Last Sunday, Nvidia’s board of directors said it was launching an investigation into Huang being the target of an alleged Chinese spy, with whom he had an affair. Huang admitted to the affair in an email to Nvidia employees and said he is cooperating with the investigation. Reports have identified Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at tech firm Megaspeed, as the woman he had the relationship with. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry,” Jensen Huang said in a statement. The New York Times reported Wednesday that Huang also had an affair with Kimberly Powell, a married Nvidia executive who reported directly to him. Powell, Nvidia’s vice president of healthcare, joined the company in 2008. On Thursday, Reuters reported that Huang also had an “intimate relationship” with another Nvidia employee. Reuters did not identify the woman, and Nvidia declined to comment. Rep. Brian Mast, the Republican chairman of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, told reporters Thursday that Huang had agreed to testify before Congress after being threatened with a subpoena. House Republicans have asked Huang to sit for a closed-door interview on Dec. 1, CNBC reported . Here’s what we know so far, and why the scandal matters. First, who is Jensen Huang? Jensen Huang founded Nvidia, one of the biggest makers of specialized computer chips in the world. Its chips were first designed for computer graphics, but demand for Nvidia’s hardware has skyrocketed with the AI boom of the past few years. China and the U.S. are in a heated competition for AI technology, and that includes access to chips like the ones Nvidia makes. Huang is an American citizen who was born in Taiwan. He founded Nvidia in 1993 and served as its president and CEO until Thursday. What we know about the Huang affair so far According to the New York Times , it’s unclear when Jensen Huang met Alice Huang, but the two were photographed together in 2024 at a bar in Taipei, Taiwan. That was roughly when Megaspeed, the AI company she worked for, began its push into the AI sector. News reports have not confirmed whether Alice Huang still works at Megaspeed. Megaspeed has touted its membership in Nvidia’s partnership program, which would give it access to Nvidia’s latest technology. Huang apologized for the affair in a message to Nvidia employees and asked for privacy for his family. “I take full responsibility for what I did and the hurt I caused,” Huang wrote, “and I accept the criticism that comes with it.” He pledged to earn back his employees’ confidence and said he was cooperating fully with the board’s investigation. “I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America’s national security,” he wrote. The New York Times reported that U.S. intelligence officials believe Alice Huang was gathering information for the Chinese government. China denied that it was spying , calling the allegation unsubstantiated. “It is nothing but smears against China,” a Ministry of Foreign Affairs spokesperson said. The New York Times also reported that Nvidia executives contacted the U.S. Commerce Department last year seeking information about the department’s investigation into Megaspeed. The investigation was later transferred to the Justice Department, which is reportedly looking into whether Megaspeed illegally routed Nvidia products into China. Why this matters AI is the biggest thing in tech right now, from chatbots like ChatGPT and Claude to software development and bioengineering. Governments are trying to work out how to use AI for security and across the economy, and China and the U.S. are racing to lead its development. The technology has moved so fast that some CEOs of AI companies have suggested a pause before it develops beyond what humans can control. Nvidia has contracts with the U.S. government to use its technology in several areas , and Huang has a close relationship with President Trump. U.S. officials are trying to determine whether the affair allowed the Chinese government to obtain information about Nvidia’s technology and its agreements with the U.S. government. Nvidia’s board said in its statement that it does not believe national security or company secrets were compromised. Trump said last Sunday that he considers Huang “a fine person” who should stay on as CEO of Nvidia. “I think he probably has an excuse for it. We’ll have to hear it,” Trump told reporters. “He’s done an amazing job for our country.” On Tuesday, the New York Times reported that Secretary of State Marco Rubio, who is also national security adviser, told Trump in May that the U.S. believed Huang was involved with a woman suspected of being a Chinese spy. Trump received the information aboard Air Force One en route to a summit in China, the Times reported. Huang went with the president on that trip. The Times said it was not the first time Trump had been told about U.S. intelligence on the affair. articles.title: Sean Duffy is imploring Congress for FAA funding. Dems say the agency already has it.
articles.summary: A traveler walks with luggage near the air traffic control tower at Los Angeles International Airport (LAX) on November 12, 2025 in Los Angeles, California. - Mario Tama/Getty Images Following a historic airspace meltdown on Friday that grounded all flights nationwide, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has implored Congress to authorize tens of billions of dollars in additional funding for the Federal Aviation Administration. But Democrats, who are set to take the majority in January, are pointing to  legislation passed by Republicans last year that already gave the agency $12.5 billion, arguing that it already has the funds it needs. Duffy says that’s not true. “I have no money in that $12.5 billion that I can use for a new architecture for telecom. I can’t build new software to manage our airplanes in the airspace because it dates back to the 1990s, but there’s no money for that. There’s no money for towers. Our towers are old,” Duffy said on CNN’s “State of the Union” with Dana Bash on Sunday. Duffy had asked Congress for around $30 billion but after Friday’s incident, he upped the request to $50 billion. President Donald Trump, in a social media post on Sunday, also urged Congress to “give the money, FAST!” The transportation secretary said the ground stop was likely due to an issue that occurred while contractor L3Harris was switching an old copper wire at an air traffic location in El Dorado, Arkansas, to a more modern fiber optic system. It is unclear whether the outage was due to faulty equipment or contractor error. Of the $12.5 billion given to the agency for three years under Trump’s massive spending and policy bill — which no Democrats supported — $4.75 billion was allocated for “telecommunications infrastructure modernization and systems upgrades.” Duffy said at a news conference Saturday that the agency has spent about one-third of the modernization budget so far. On Sunday, Duffy said all the telecom work can be done by “the first part of 2029.” unknown content item - “All I need is the money to finish it. And my, my hope is that if they give me money today, I’ll be going tomorrow to build it,” Duffy said. Later Saturday, Reps. Rick Larsen and André Carson — the top Democrats on two House panels overseeing the aviation industry — asked the administration to explain to Congress why the agency needs more money if there are still unspent funds. The two added in a joint statement that FAA and DOT employees will brief their staff on Monday. Meanwhile, some Democrats slammed the administration’s priorities and how it has spent money in immigration enforcement and construction projects in Washington, DC, over aviation modernization and safety. “There is a pot of 60 billion extra dollars on top of the regularly appropriated amount for ICE and we should use at least a portion of that money for the FAA,” Hawaii Sen. Brian Schatz said in a post on X . “We can solve this problem and not spend any additional taxpayer dollars.” Illinois Sen. Tammy Duckworth said in a post on X , “You’ve literally controlled Congress for the past two years. And apparently, there’s always been money for vanity projects. But none to fix our air traffic control system? Perhaps Trump should prioritize aviation safety over his pathetic Arch.” Rep. Rosa DeLauro, the House Appropriations Committee’s top Democrat, called Duffy’s $50 billion request a “ransom.” “Our air traffic controllers have been failed by Secretary Duffy,” DeLauro said in a post on X, adding, “We need a competent partner at DOT.” However, Maryland Sen. Chris Van Hollen, a Democrat who launched a bid for Senate majority leader last week, signaled openness to supporting additional funds for the agency on Sunday while calling on administration officials to come to Congress and “justify” the ask. “I will support whatever level of money is necessary to fix this problem. We should fix this problem on a bipartisan basis,” Hollen told CNN on Sunday, but added, “It’s really rich to hear the secretary pointing the fingers at Congress when Congress has given the administration what they asked for. If they need more, they should come up and justify it.” Sen. Chris Van Hollen (D-Maryland) speaks with reporters as he boards a vehicle to depart the US Capitol on November 12, 2026. - Francis Chung/POLITICO/AP Republicans could use the remaining weeks of their majority to approve additional funding for the agency, and outgoing House Speaker Mike Johnson said Saturday that he would add FAA funding to an upcoming “legislative package.” “We don’t really need any investigation to understand we need further investment,” Johnson told Fox News. “We’re going to work to get it done.” It was not immediately clear to congressional aides how leaders will pass new funding. Currently, appropriators are negotiating a government funding deal ahead of a December 11 deadline. Senate leadership aides in each party did not immediately respond to questions about the path forward in that chamber. GOP Sen. Eric Schmitt is also pushing for passage of his bill, the Modern Skies Act , which would invest $30 billion in modernizing the nation’s aviation system. The Missouri senator spoke with Trump on Friday, and has also spoken with Duffy and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin on the topic. CNN’s Ellis Kim, Ted Barrett, Logan Schiciano, Isa Mudannayake and Aleena Fayaz contributed to this report. articles.title: Trump's handpicked party chair faces a rebellion in wake of midterm losses
articles.summary: NEW YORK (AP) — A nascent rebellion is underway against President Donald Trump's handpicked chairman at the Republican National Committee, and it’s already getting ugly. Some members are calling for a forensic audit of spending decisions, including hair and makeup services for Trump and other officials, as well as the hiring of the daughter of Trump's former chief of staff. Feuding Republicans are leaking emails and opposition research on rival factions. The White House is threatening to cut off fundraising assistance if the rebels don’t fall in line. The emerging fight, which will shape the 2028 presidential nominating contest, represents a rare challenge to Trump's dominance, even after the party's worst midterm performance in a generation. Despite the broad losses, Republican leaders across Washington have shown little desire to move past Trump and have largely stood behind his most unpopular policies. But inside the Republican National Committee, an organization of 168 members elected from every state who oversee the party’s national political operation, a small and growing collection of concerned Republicans are backing an attempt to depose Joe Gruters. Trump wants to keep him in charge. The dissidents are rallying behind Kentucky’s KC Crosbie, the RNC's second-in-command. She launched her bid just two days after the Nov. 3 election in a letter that drew the fury of both the White House and Gruters' allies. Crosbie remains a vocal Trump supporter who backs his “Make America Great Again” agenda, but her opponents view her gambit as a direct challenge to the president and his power. “Our job is to elect Republicans broadly, not to support one man all the time," said RNC member Oscar Brock of Tennessee, who is supporting Crosbie’s candidacy. He said that requires a change in leadership because “there’s so much frustration that Chairman Gruters didn’t pull his weight in this election.” In her letter, Crosbie described the midterms as “a serious setback" and called for the RNC to provide “an honest account” of what went wrong. Crosbie declined to be interviewed. The leadership election will be held in January at the RNC’s winter meeting in Arizona. Inside the rebellion against Gruters Some would-be Crosbie supporters privately acknowledge they're worried about a backlash from the White House, especially with Stephen Miller taking over as Trump's chief of staff. Others believe in the committee's tradition of having presidents pick their own party chiefs. Gruters also has vocal backers. Lauren LePage, an RNC member from Maine, praised Gruters' leadership and efforts to help her father, Paul LePage, flip a congressional seat — a rare bright spot for Republicans this cycle. “From my perspective, as chairman, he did his job," she said, adding that Trump's endorsement is “something that the committee should take very seriously.” The Republicans who have lined up behind Crosbie insist a leadership change is needed to send a clear message that the party will do things differently after losses even in Republican strongholds like Texas , South Carolina and Mississippi . Patti Lyman, an RNC member from Virginia, said it would be “catastrophic” and “insulting” to the party’s base “to keep the same leadership and pretend that we don’t need to do anything different, that we don’t need new players and a new plan.” Sue Cienki, an RNC committee member from Rhode Island, predicted that Crosbie would have the backing of at least two members from 10 states — a total of 20 — at the committee's January meeting. That's the minimum required for a successful nomination. Trump is furious with Crosbie Trump and senior White House officials were livid about Crosbie’s Nov. 5 letter and the fact that they were given no heads-up. The president soon released a lengthy statement on his Truth Social social media platform hailing Gruters as a “MAGA Warrior” and giving him his “Complete and Total Endorsement.” Trump is expected to play a central role in picking the party's next presidential nominee. The party's future is at stake Allies of Gruters say a leadership change now would put the RNC at a severe disadvantage heading into the next presidential cycle because a new team would need time to get up to speed. They say friction between the president and the committee's leadership would curtail their ability to organize and raise money. They also reject Crosbie's call for a postelection review, which they said would do little more than consume six months rehashing the past and put all their grievances on paper. Gruters spent much of this week holding private phone conversations with committee members. Those who participated in the calls said Gruters listened to their grievances, but said little about what he would do differently. Spending faces scrutiny The opposition to Gruters has focused on the RNC's spending decisions under him. Republicans had a massive fundraising advantage and still had deep losses. “There’s clearly a groundswell of support for a forensic audit,” said Brock, the RNC member from Tennessee. In a letter to RNC members sent Thursday night and obtained by The Associated Press, Gruters acknowledged concerns about spending and other issues. Gruters defended a $22,500 expenditure for hospitality space at the Presidents Cup, a golf event, saying the space was offered to major donors and "resulted in $2.5 million in renewed contributions to the RNC.” He also addressed “a brief contract” between the RNC and Caroline Wiles, a longtime Republican consultant, who is the daughter of Susie Wiles, Trump's former chief of staff. Gruters said she was hired by his predecessor at the committee, Michael Whatley. “While I have no reason to doubt Caroline Wiles’s value to the RNC or Chairman Whatley’s reasons for bringing her on, this was a brief six-month engagement that ended when I was elected Chairman,” he wrote. Gruters also defended the RNC's decision to pay for “hair and make-up services” for senior White House officials, including Trump, Vice President JD Vance and former press secretary Karoline Leavitt. “This was a request made of us so that the expense did not fall to taxpayers,” Gruters wrote, adding that the beneficiaries “generously gave so much of their limited time and energies to help the RNC this cycle” and “did not ask for much of us in return, so we felt this was a request we could accommodate.” This article originally appeared on Associated Press at https://www.yahoo.com/news/politics/articles/trumps-handpicked-party-chair-faces-192048723.html

articles.title: Russian diesel under Trump deal struggles to reach U.S. market amid legal fears and criticism
articles.summary: A general view shows a refinery in Volgograd, Russia, April 22, 2022. - Reuters/File More than a month after President Donald Trump announced a surprise deal to import Russian diesel , the oil has struggled to reach the US market amid outrage and legal concerns. Several oil tankers that departed from a key Russian oil-loading port — and are believed to be laden with diesel — are no longer bound for the US, according to ship tracking data from MarineTraffic, and US businesses and ports have steered clear of accepting Russian diesel for fear of legal and reputational risks, experts told CNN. Bipartisan lawmakers and European allies expressed outrage at the agreement that Trump said he reached with Russian President Vladimir Putin to bring tens of thousands of barrels of Russian diesel into US and global markets. They condemned it as a concession to Russia as it continued its war against Ukraine and warned that those who imported the diesel could run afoul of international sanctions and US law. One of the tankers, Agioi Fanendes , departed Russia with tens of thousands of barrels of Russian diesel. Its destination was listed as the Port of New York and New Jersey, and it was initially expected to arrive around November 7. As of Sunday, the vessel was hovering hundreds of miles off the eastern coast of the US. It was officially broadcasting “FOR ORDERS” instead of a destination port. A spokesperson for Eastern Mediterranean Maritime Limited, the company that operates the tanker, told CNN on Thursday that its “discharging port is not confirmed yet.” Several other oil tankers that departed Primorsk — one of Russia’s largest oil-loading ports — in mid-October have also shifted away from the US, according to data from MarineTraffic reviewed by CNN. One, the Talisman, docked at the Port of Alexandria in Egypt in recent days. Another, the Leruo, is now heading to Brazil. They had earlier declared their destinations as the US Atlantic coast. Both vessels are under European and British sanctions, and the Talisman is also sanctioned in the US. A White House official told CNN on Wednesday that “consistent with the deal agreed to between President Trump and President Putin, Russian diesel is on the water and heading to the market, which will ease prices for Americans.” The official did not say the diesel was heading to the US. The person said the deal “was made to add diesel supply to the global market — lowering prices for Americans and the world — which is exactly what will be done.” Trump announced in a social media post on October 9 that he had reached a deal with Putin for Russia to “immediately supply over 300,000 Tons of Diesel Fuel to the American and Global Marketplace.” The administration billed the deal, which was announced weeks before the US midterm elections amid steep fuel costs, as a way to lower prices for US consumers. Experts said the diesel would have little to no impact on prices, and amounts to less than a day of US energy consumption. Questions about legality of importing Russian fuel Last month, a group of bipartisan lawmakers sent letters to the CEOs of JPMorgan Chase, Bank of America, Citigroup, Wells Fargo, Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley, and the heads of Port Authorities of New York/New Jersey and of Houston, Corpus Christi and Beaumont, Texas, warning that they could face legal action if they are involved in importing the Russian diesel into the US. The Ending Importation of Russian Oil Act of 2022 bans Russian-origin energy products, including diesel fuel, from being imported into the US “unless — following a period for consultation with Congress — the President certifies to Congress that Russia has ceased military hostilities in Ukraine, that Russia poses no immediate military threat to NATO members, and that Russia recognizes the right of Ukrainians to choose their government,” the lawmakers warned . Although the US Treasury Department issued a sanctions waiver to allow the import of the diesel under the deal between the Trump administration and Moscow, the lawmakers consider that sanctions waiver to defy the law. “Any importation of Russian diesel into the U.S. raises significant legal questions and may be subject to legal action, as well as congressional investigations,” wrote Democratic Sens. Jeanne Shaheen, Ron Wyden, Sheldon Whitehouse, Chris Coons, Elizabeth Warren, GOP Sen. Thom Tillis, and Democratic Rep. Gregory Meeks. “Criminal penalties may apply to any company that knowingly buys Russian diesel or facilitates its importation, and not simply the importer of record,” they wrote. New Jersey Gov. Mikie Sherrill warned her state’s port and terminal operators last week that “any effort to profit from the illegal trade in Russian fuel will be met with harsh penalties.” Charles Lichfield, the director of economic foresight and analysis and the C. Boyden Gray senior fellow at the Atlantic Council’s GeoEconomics Center, noted that US importers would face “the immediate reputational risk” as well as the legal ramifications. He noted that a general license from the Treasury Department, which allows businesses to import the diesel without fear of sanctions, would appear to be good protection but the 2022 law is still on the books, which raises questions about legality and the potential for prosecution down the line. “All of this is very politically charged (and) the volumes are small,” he said. “You could make a few million dollars off this shipment, but is it really worth it?” Julian Hayda, the associate director for advocacy at the organization Razom for Ukraine, noted that “now that Democrats have control of both chambers of Congress, they are most certainly going to launch investigations into these companies, so it’s not going to be worth it for many of these companies to buy this vehicle in and when it arrives on American shores.” This story has been updated with additional information. articles.title: Violent 20- to 30-foot waves pound the West Coast as storms continue
articles.summary: Much of the West Coast continues to face hazardous coastal conditions on Sunday, including 20- to 30-foot waves slamming waterfront communities. Coastal impacts are expected Sunday along nearly the entire length of the West Coast, from Southern California to the Northwest states, as a series of storms fuel widespread dangerous rough surf. The latest storm system has moved into the Pacific Northwest, bringing another round of rain and mountain snow from Northern California to Washington and Oregon. Stephen Lam/San Francisco Chronicle via Getty Images - PHOTO: Bystanders react after being caught in a sneaker wave along Beach Boulevard near the Pacifica Pier in Pacifica, Calif., Nov. 14, 2026. But the primary concern on Sunday will be focused on the persistent rough surf and large waves across much of the West Coast amid back-to-back storms. High surf alerts remained in effect on Sunday along much of the West Coast. ABC News - PHOTO: High surf advisories and warnings stretch nearly the entire length of the West Coast, November 15, 2026. Dangerous, large breaking waves of 20 to 30 feet in height are expected to continue along the Northern California, Oregon and Washington coasts before easing on Monday. Kevin Carter/Getty Images - PHOTO:A surfer rides a large wave in the Pacific Ocean off the coast of La Jolla as El Niño-fueled ocean temperatures in the mid-70s continue to break records, November 14, 2026, in San Diego, California. The large waves will create hazardous conditions along the coast, with waves inundating beaches and potentially bringing significant beach erosion and damage. ABC News - PHOTO: Rough surf and windy conditions are forecast for the West Coast from San Francisco to the Northwest through Monday morning, November 16, 2026. Periods of rain along the Pacific Northwest Coast will spread inland across the Intermountain West and Northern California. ABC News - PHOTO: The forecast calls for rough surf and windy conditions along the West Coast from San Francisco to the Northwest through Tuesday afternoon. Some of the highest elevations of the Cascade Mountains could see some snow as well. Meanwhile, a new system is expected to bring more unsettled weather to the Pacific Northwest Coast by early Wednesday. Heavy rain in southeast Texas Widespread showers and storms are forecast across southeastern Texas on Sunday, with isolated downpours possible. Localized flash flooding could develop where the heaviest rain moves through, including metropolitan Houston, Galveston and Freeport. Rainfall totals of 1 to 2 inches are forecast across the region, with isolated amounts up to 4 inches possible through Sunday night. How El Nino and a persistent marine heat wave are affecting West Coast wildlife Storms in southeast Texas are expected to bring heavy rain, with 1 to 2 inches possible across most of the region and some areas receiving 4 to 6 inches. ABC News - PHOTO: Rounds of rain expected from Texas to Louisiana, November 15, 2026. The weather system hitting southeast Texas is also bringing windy conditions along the coast, with gusts of up to 40 mph possible, leading authorities to warn residents about the potential of falling tree limbs and scattered power outages. articles.title: Bill Cassidy, both a doctor and senator, calls for Trump to replace Kennedy at HHS
articles.summary: Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., speaks to members of the media on April 29, 2021, in Washington, D.C. (Stefani Reynolds/Getty Images) Sen. Bill Cassidy, R-La., called Sunday for President Donald Trump to replace Health and Human Services Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., saying his handling of measles, rising healthcare costs, and ultraprocessed foods amounts to a series of failures. "If I were president, I would choose someone else because there needs to be accountability for higher healthcare costs, more measles deaths, losing elimination status, and no progress on processed foods," Cassidy told CBS' "Face the Nation." Cassidy, a physician who chairs the Senate Health, Education, Labor and Pensions Committee, said Kennedy's record could damage Trump's legacy unless the president changes course. "The American voters signaled at the midterm they don't like status quo, particularly in healthcare. And I think it's time for something different," he said. His criticism followed a recording played during the interview in which Kennedy said the Senate would no longer have leverage over him after Democrats take control in January. "The Senate no longer has any leverage over me and, you know, that's a big deal," Kennedy said. "Then we have [Trump chief of staff] Steve Miller, who is a friend of our movement, and I don't think anything is going to get in our way now." Cassidy dismissed that reasoning, saying Kennedy was "obviously trying to provide cover for failure as secretary of health and human services." He said mothers who supported Kennedy had expected action on ultraprocessed foods but had seen minimal progress. Hundreds contacted Cassidy during the debate over whether he should support Kennedy's confirmation, he said. "They have every right to be disappointed," Cassidy said. He also pointed to small businesses dropping health coverage and employees struggling to afford deductibles. "This has been a failure," he said. Asked whether Kennedy should face impeachment, Cassidy emphasized Trump's responsibility for deciding whether to keep him. "As regards impeachment, you know, you can impeach, I guess, over a ham sandwich. They will have to decide what to do on that," he said. "I do think it's more importantly the president's decision." Cassidy also called for stronger public messaging about vaccination after host Margaret Brennan cited reporting that the United States had lost its measles elimination status. He warned that people who choose not to get vaccinated can expose infants too young to receive the vaccine and people with weakened immune systems to measles. "If you have not been vaccinated, you could be the person that brings death to another," Cassidy said. "That's something to remember." He said the administration should repeatedly emphasize those risks. "I think that should be the message going out. It should be pounded, pounded, pounded," he said. Cassidy said he remains in regular contact with the director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, but the limited time remaining before the end of the congressional session could complicate scheduling a public hearing. He cited his recent exchange with the director about a broken online tool for locating flu shots as an example of oversight taking place outside hearings. Cassidy also declined to predict whether his committee would advance the nomination of Dr. Heidi Overton, Trump's choice to lead the Food and Drug Administration, in a vote scheduled for Wednesday. Trump nominated Overton in September. "I've been working the phones all week. Speaking with Overton, speaking with others, I still have questions," he said. Brennan noted Cassidy had previously described Overton's role in developing the administration's childhood vaccine policies as almost disqualifying. Cassidy said senators must weigh their concerns against the possibility of leaving the FDA under a succession of temporary leaders who could be more susceptible to Kennedy's influence. A permanent commissioner could establish greater independence, he said. "It continues to be back and forth, and we will know Wednesday," Cassidy said. On Social Security, Cassidy expressed frustration over the prospects for advancing legislation before year's end, accusing Senate Finance Committee ranking member Ron Wyden, D-Ore., of resisting a hearing. Cassidy said Senate Majority Leader John Thune, R-S.D., and Finance Committee Chair Mike Crapo, R-Idaho, had committed to a hearing and committee vote on a Social Security bill. Trump also had personally committed his support, Cassidy said. His proposal would borrow $1.5 trillion to establish an investment fund separate from the Social Security trust fund, allowing the money to grow over six decades to help address the program's long-term financing needs. Cassidy said Wyden opposes investing taxpayer money in the stock market but contended that a similar approach had succeeded for the federal railroad retirement system. He said he was willing to consider other proposals, including one from Sen. Bernie Sanders, I-Vt. "Congress is there to take tough choices, and now those tough choices are being ducked," Cassidy said. © 2026 Newsmax. articles.summary: 全球制造、公用事业与矿业企业自今年6月以来市值合计蒸发4.2万亿美元， 这场抛售几乎抹去了此前12个月内同类企业所积累的9.4万亿美元涨幅的近半数， 曾风靡一时的AI“卖铲”交易正在急速逆转。 据英国《金融时报》分析，在媒体报道中与数据中心建设关联度越高的企业，遭受的冲击越为惨烈。投资者对AI热潮的信心正在动摇，从适配超大规模数据中心的燃气发电机组制造商，到连接AI服务器机架所需的高端光纤企业，此前被争相追捧的标的如今纷纷遭到抛售。工业板块已成为今夏以来标普500指数中表现第二差的板块，仅次于科技板块。 市场的转向折射出更广泛的担忧： 超大规模云计算企业持续以债务融资推高资本开支，叠加美国国内对数据中心建设日益高涨的政治阻力，令投资者开始质疑这场建设热潮能否持续。 龙头企业市值腰斩 数据中心燃气发电机组的主要供应商卡特彼勒（Caterpillar）过去六个月跌幅超过30%，而自6月30日股价触及历史高点以来，市值已缩水214亿美元，跌幅达44%。 此外，核电企业Oklo尽管在今年1月与Meta签署了供电合同，股价仍重挫49%。暖通空调系统制造商Comfort Systems与光纤制造商康宁（Corning）在同一时期均损失了约一半市值。 据英国金融时报称，德意志银行高级美国经济学家Brett Ryan表示， 此前有大量机构资金“盲目涌入”这些交易，“可能助推了部分企业过于乐观的估值” 。他还指出， 股票市场正在“向信贷市场早已发出的信号靠拢”——后者对数据中心建设中风险融资的增长早有警示。 风险投资人、麻省理工学院研究员Paul Kedrosky则直言，投资者将传统工业企业当作半导体股票来对待，本身就是一个错误。 “在与对冲基金和家族办公室的讨论中，‘一切都是成长股’这种论调无处不在——这当然是荒谬的。” 不过，尽管股价承压，多家企业的经营基本面依然稳健。美国政府最新数据显示，截至今年9月的12个月内，美国数据中心建设支出（不含IT设备与芯片）达到960亿美元。 第三季度业绩同样印证了需求的韧性。 卡特彼勒报告积压订单达创纪录的780亿美元，其发电业务销售额同比增长75%，主要由数据中心需求驱动。 西门子来自数据中心的电气设备订单积压在2026年增长60%，达到70亿欧元；伊顿（Eaton）同类订单则实现同比翻倍。多家燃气轮机制造商表示，2026年前九个月已斩获数十亿美元订单。 Dell'Oro Group分析师Alex Cordovil表示，“就这些企业的营收基本面和潜在盈利前景而言，我们仍然看到非常强劲的预期。”他补充道，电气化和供应链重构等更宏观的趋势持续支撑着众多工业企业的核心业务，“建设并未减速……积压订单处于历史高位，这意味着至少到2027年，营收增长已基本锁定。” 工业控制设备制造商Allient首席执行官Richard S Warzala在11月5日的业绩电话会上表示，对AI的需求不会下滑。 “即便对新数据中心的建设实施暂停令，那些已经开工的项目也必须完成。” 此外，Kedrosky对订单积压数据持保留态度，认为这是滞后指标，反映的是此前的预期，而非当下的真实需求。他指出，企业存在"双重乃至三重下单"的现象——为了在感知到的供应紧缺中抢占排队位置而超额备货。 Brett Ryan的判断则更为直接：股票市场正在完成一次迟来的估值校正，向信贷市场早已传递的风险信号对齐。这场历时数月、市值蒸发逾4万亿美元的调整，本质上是资本市场对"一切皆成长股"叙事的系统性重新定价。 中期选举后的监管不确定性 此次抛售的另一重要背景，是美国中期选举后数据中心监管政策走向的不明朗。 在本月的中期选举中，对数据中心建设实施限制的提案获得了美国选民的广泛支持，但其实际影响目前仍不明朗。 花旗研究在选举后发布的报告中指出，尽管预计更严格的监管将给数据中心行业带来更多波动，但大范围限制建设的可能性仍然较低。 星座能源（Constellation Energy）首席执行官Joseph Dominguez表示，选举后的市场反应是“过度反应”，并强调民主党人“非常在意”保护数据中心的蓝领就业岗位。 德意志银行的Ryan则认为，即便部分地区出台禁令，也只会将建设需求转移至监管更为宽松的地区。 “归根结底，如果市场对这些设施存在需求，它们终将在某个地方建成。” 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 如何定价“政府债取消免税”
articles.summary: 11月11日，央行发布三季度货币政策执行报告，设专栏《国际利率水平比较》，其中明确指出“国债免征所得税使纳税投资者愿意接受低于应税债券的收益率”，“比较利率时需还原税收因素的影响”。 这一表态，让政府债利息所得税免税取消的预期再度升温。政金债、二级资本债、永续债、信用债随即出现不同程度的调整。消息发布后，10年国债中债估值单日上行0.7BP，政金债调整幅度更为明显——11月11日至13日，10年国开债收益率累计上行7.5BP，与国债利差由5.2BP走阔至11.0BP。 11月16日今日，国债期货普遍走弱，30年国债期货跌超0.5%，10年期国债期货跌0.13%。 而这不是央行第一次表态。2025年一季度货币政策执行报告曾提及税收制度影响国债利率基准作用，约12周后，政府债利息增值税即恢复征收。 但值得注意的是，这一轮的市场分歧已经发生了变化。华泰证券固收团队在11月14日发布的研报中指出， 当前讨论的核心已从“是否取消政府债利息企业所得税免税”，转向“如何取消、何时取消、影响多大”。 “政府债取消免税”讨论再度升温 华泰证券固收团队在研报中梳理了2024年以来的时间线：2024年8月，市场曾出现“监管拟取消利率债基、信用债基免税”的预期；2025年8月，政府债利息增值税免税被取消，确立了“新老划断”的操作先例；2026年8月至今，讨论焦点转向国债、地方债利息企业所得税。 此轮讨论的直接导火索，是三季度货币政策执行报告专栏。华泰研究注意到，央行在2025年一季度货币政策执行报告中曾指出，“债券市场税收制度设计也会对债券市场价格形成和国债利率基准作用的发挥产生影响”，此后不久，政府债利息增值税免税即宣告取消。 “央行的表态与政策落地存在先后关系。”华泰研究在报告中写道。 按25%税率还原，2026年11月13日10年国债收益率1.61%对应的应税等价收益率约2.15%，高于10年国开债收益率1.72%。 华泰研究认为，央行推动取消政府债免税主要有四方面原因：免税影响国债利率基准作用的发挥；利率比较需还原税收影响；国债收益率曲线在货币政策框架中的地位上升；以及全额免征国债利息企业所得税在主要经济体中并不多见。 调整路径：地方债或先行，国债等修法 国债的免税依据是《企业所得税法》第二十六条，取消需要修改这部法律，须经全国人大常委会审议；地方债的免税依据是财税〔2013〕5号文，属于部门规范性文件，经国务院批准后由财政部和国家税务总局发文即可调整，无需修法，也无需公开征求意见。 这一法律层级的差异，直接决定了调整节奏的差异。 国盛证券固收团队在研报中指出，“取消免税，本质上是对两部法律的修改，属于国家立法机关的职权范围”，“走完整个流程通常也需要数月乃至更长时间”。 华泰研究的判断是： 基准情形为“新老划断、地方债先行、国债随修法跟进”。地方债调整无需修法，未来数月需关注财税部门公告；国债调整的关键在于2027年度立法工作计划。 新发政府债收益率：10-20BP还是9.1BP？ 取消免税后新发政府债收益率将上行多少，是市场分歧最大的问题。 华泰证券从四个角度推演新发10年期政府债的收益率上行幅度。 上限：约54BP。 若自营机构要求完全传导，维持现有税后收益所需的名义收益率需上行54BP（收益率×25%/(1-25%)）；30年地方债对应的理论补偿为74BP，对应的价格损失约16%。这是极端上限。 下限：约10BP。 国开债利息需缴纳企业所得税而国债免税，二者信用资质相近，10年国开债与国债利差长期被视为隐含税率的反映。当前这一利差的隐含税率已远低于法定25%，原因在于公募基金等产品层面免税的资金主导了国开债的边际定价。若新发国债向国开债收敛，新发10年国债收益率上行约10BP。 参照系：增值税新老划断经验。 2025年8月增值税调整后，10年国债新老券利差月均约4.8BP，更靠近资管产品3%档的理论税差，而非自营机构6%档的理论值。这说明应税新券主要由交易盘定价，税负较重的自营机构倾向于持有存量免税老券。 综合判断： 华泰证券预计，随着应税利率债规模逐年扩大、免税资金承接能力被稀释，隐含税率可能回升至6%-11%（大致对应2021-2022年水平），对应新发10年国债收益率上行约10-20BP，30年国债上行约15-25BP。 国盛证券则提出了另一套框架——税负分摊法。 分析师杨业伟等指出，取消免税的本质是债券体系每年多承担一笔确定金额的税款，可精确计算，无需假设供需弹性。按2026年新增政府债约26万亿元、1.6%利率计，年利息约4091亿元，25%税率对应首年税负约1023亿元。 假设由新发政府债、政金债、信用债等约112万亿受影响债券共同分摊，利率冲击中枢约9.1BP/年。 国盛证券强调，40BP是"税负完全由新券独力承担"的极端边界，而分摊法下税负由体量约四倍的整个债券体系共同吸收，单位冲击自然被稀释。两份报告从不同角度出发，区间下限趋于一致，均认为实际调整幅度将大幅低于理论上限。 各方如何博弈 财政方面，华泰研究测算，新老划断下取消免税后第1年财政净增收约210亿元，第10年约1904亿元。 但这一收益存在临界点——收益率上行超过约40BP时，财政净增收转负。 地方政府方面 ，情况更为复杂。地方债利息由地方承担，而取消免税后新增的企业所得税多归中央与总部所在地。华泰研究测算，地方本级财政的盈亏平衡点不超过16BP——地方债收益率上行超过这一幅度，地方本级财政即由净增收转为净减收。"取消地方债免税可能加重欠发达地区的利息负担"，华泰研究在报告中写道，"多付的利息难以通过税收收回，形成财力由欠发达地区向发达地区的转移。" 银行保险方面，是成本的主要承担者。 2026年9月末，商业银行持有银行间市场国债的70.6%、地方债的71.7%。华泰研究测算，以10年国债收益率1.61%、大型银行计息负债付息率约1.3%测算，若取消所得税免税，持有新券的税后净贡献将由约55BP降至约17BP，下降约38BP。保险方面，新发30年地方债相对普通型人身险2.0%预定利率上限的税后利差，将由约58BP收窄至约6BP。 为何政金债和信用债跌得更多？ 11月11日至13日，10年国开债收益率累计上行7.5BP，10年国债收益率仅上行1.6BP，10年国开债与国债利差由5.0BP走阔至11.0BP。 国盛证券对此的解释是：“它们在为税收冲击进行补涨式定价，或者说，在为过去过度压缩的利差'还债'。” 逻辑在于：政金债、信用债本身的税收政策没有任何变化，但当作为定价锚的政府债新券利率因征税预期上行时，这些品种与新券的相对性价比被动恶化，原本已极薄的利差不足以覆盖锚上移带来的重估压力，于是引发跟随上行。 华泰研究则从利差结构的角度分析了各品种的走向： 期限利差方面，30年与10年国债利差面临走阔压力——取消免税所需的名义收益率补偿与收益率水平成正比，超长端久期更长，完全补偿对应的价格损失约为10年国债的3倍。 新老券利差方面，存量免税老券的稀缺性上升，新老券利差将在增值税税差的基础上进一步走阔。 信用利差方面，信用债与国债的利差将收窄——税收利差消失，向信用债与政金债的利差收敛。 铁道债则是个例外——铁道债利息减半征收企业所得税，不受本次可能的税收调整影响，取消政府债免税后，铁道债相对国债由税收劣势转为税收优势。 机构行为将如何重塑 取消免税后，银行、保险与公募基金的配置逻辑将出现分化。 华泰研究测算，银行首年多缴企业所得税约321亿元，相当于2025年商业银行净利润2.38万亿元的1.3%；按线性替换的简化假设，约11年后升至3084亿元左右（13.0%）。 银行配置行为的变化或包括：存量免税老券的稀缺性上升，银行持有老券至到期的意愿增强；参与新发政府债一级投标时，要求更高的发行利率；超长政府债的配置意愿进一步下降；在利率债内部，政金债与铁道债的相对价值上升。 对于保险而言，偿二代下的资本占用限制了向铁道债、政金债和信用债的平移。华泰研究认为，保险“更可能提高超长政府债的买入利率要求”。 公募基金方面，华泰研究指出了一个值得关注的问题：取消政府债免税后，自营机构经由公募基金持有10年国债的税后收益率较直接持有高约42BP，“税收扭曲由免税券种与应税券种之间，转移至直接投资与基金投资之间”。 “需要关注公募基金分红免税问题何时提上日程。”华泰研究在报告中写道，“若取消政府债利息免税，为避免税源经由基金渠道流失、维持税制的一致性，机构取得的基金分红免税安排可能成为政策调整的下一个方向。” 关键时间节点 华泰研究梳理了需要关注的时间节点：未来数月，需关注财政部、国家税务总局是否发布地方债利息企业所得税调整公告；2026年12月下旬，全国人大常委会会议是否对征管法修订草案进行二审；2027年3月，全国人民代表大会会议政府工作报告与预算报告的相关表述；2027年4-5月，全国人大常委会年度立法工作计划是否列入企业所得税法修改。 “货币政策执行报告的表态与政策落地之间存在时差。”华泰研究写道，“2025年5月9日一季度货币政策执行报告发布，约12周后的8月1日，财政部和国家税务总局即公告恢复征收政府债利息增值税。2026年11月11日三季度报告专栏再次讨论国债免税，机械参照上述时差，未来数月是需要关注的窗口，但所得税调整比增值税复杂，实际时差可能更长。” 风险提示及免责条款 articles.title: 堪萨斯城联储施密德：通胀过高且方向错误，美联储仍有工作要做
articles.summary: 堪萨斯城联储主席施密德（Jeff Schmid）上周日（11月15日）表示，当前通胀水平令人不安，美联储仍有工作要做，但他并未明确呼吁进一步加息。这是继芝加哥联储古尔斯比、纽约联储威廉姆斯及美联储主席沃什（Kevin Warsh）相继发声后，又一位联储官员就通胀问题公开表态。 据彭博、路透和CNBC报道，施密德在夏威夷一场信贷联盟会议上发表书面讲话称，美联储偏爱的物价指标9月同比上涨 3.6% ， “令人不安地高于2%的价格稳定目标，且正朝错误方向运行” 。他援引主席沃什此前表态指出，“美联储在通胀问题上仍有工作要做，而且不幸的是，自那以后我们的工作只会更难”。 施密德今年并非联邦公开市场委员会（FOMC）投票委员。他的表态与近期市场预期方向一致——在近期通胀数据持续超预期、多位联储官员相继发出鹰派信号后，利率期货市场目前已完全消化12月会议加息25个基点的预期，并存在小概率加息50个基点的可能。 另外，波士顿联储主席Susan Collins周六也在波士顿一场住房议题会议上表示， 支持以稳健渐进的步伐推进加息 ，认为这一路径更有利于管理经济不确定性，但她同时指出，过去三个月的物价数据及劳动力市场表现，令她认为未来一年政策利率路径可能高于此前预期。 驳斥“通胀超出美联储掌控”论 施密德在讲话中着重反驳了近期市场上流行的两种叙事。 第一种叙事 认为，当前高通胀主要源于反复出现的供给冲击，与需求无关。施密德对此不认同，他表示： “通胀始终是供需失衡的结果。正是在强劲需求的背景下，供给端的扰动才会推高价格。需求始终在通胀中扮演角色，美联储通过影响需求，始终拥有应对通胀的工具和责任。” 第二种叙事 则认为，当前需求端通胀的驱动力——例如人工智能基础设施建设热潮——对货币政策免疫，加息无法有效压制。施密德同样予以反驳，称自己不认同这一判断，并强调美联储无需等待某一特定类别价格（如AI相关技术商品）作出反应，才能实现通胀目标。 他总结道： “这两种叙事有一个共同核心，即通胀在某种程度上超出了美联储的掌控。我不认为这是事实。 美联储确实拥有应对通胀的工具，也有责任实现价格稳定。 ” 通胀压力多点并发，经济基本面尚稳 施密德指出，近期通胀压力来源多元，包括能源成本上升、耐用品价格走高（部分由关税驱动）、人工智能基础设施建设以及医疗成本攀升。他特别提示，不应轻易假设生产成本上升——无论是油价上涨还是关税冲击——对通胀的影响只是暂时性的。 与此同时，施密德对经济整体状况持相对乐观态度，认为经济增长保持“稳健步伐”，失业率处于低位。他表示，劳动力市场和薪资目前似乎并未对通胀形成明显推动。 在政策操作层面，美联储9月将基准利率上调25个基点至3.75%至4.00%区间，但在10月会议上选择按兵不动。市场目前普遍预期12月会议将再度加息，1月会议亦存在进一步加息预期。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。

articles.title: 付鹏：AI叙事退潮叠加关税变量，铜价或回归2022—2023年区间【付鹏说8】
articles.summary: 《付鹏说·第七季》全新升级上线！立即订阅 AI叙事退潮叠加关税变量，铜价或回归2022—2023年区间 交易桌前看天下，付鹏说来评财经。本期视频录制2026年11月16日 今天继续和大家聊一聊铜。两三周前我在日记中专门讨论过铜的库存问题，以及COMEX一侧可能出现的情况。那篇日记之后，铜价随即破位，到目前为止的回撤幅度已经达到10%左右，并不算小。之所以现在再谈一次，是因为还有一个重要的因子尚未完全浮现出来，它未来是否会发生还不确定，但我认为有必要提前讨论。 过去几年里，如果从供需两侧综合来看，铜是大宗商品中基本面最优的品种之一，因此它一直是宏观配置中非常重要的一部分。从图上可以看到，自2022年完成估值杀跌以后，费城半导体指数与铜价的走势基本保持一致。2026年以来的约10个月时间里，二者走出了一个收敛形态：半导体板块加速见顶，从6月份自由现金流开始走弱，到10月份加速下跌，市场如今开始真正意识到，AI资本支出的叙事可能要暂停一段时间了。在这个过程中，铜价也走完了这一轮行情的末端。 铜价的高溢价从何而来：供给托底，AI叙事决定上限 这背后原因在于，过去几年铜的叙事逻辑中，需求端最重要的一条就是AI需求——电力设施、数据中心、算力中心，以及电缆、变压器、冷却系统、芯片等，AI带动了铜的需求预期。但如果放到全球范围内看，铜的需求一头在增加，另一头却在减少：中国的基建投资、房地产等领域的用铜需求是往下走的。从整个需求端来看，铜真的有那么短缺吗？其实没有。 在我看来，如果全球市场没有被割裂，2022—2023年的铜价水平更能反映全球真实的供需状况。 当然，铜的供给端确实是紧的。过去10年，上游矿山的实际资本支出基本没有扩张，铜精矿供应紧张、加工费（TC/RC）持续走低，都显示铜矿供应非常短缺，这对价格构成了重要支撑。但需要注意的是， 供给端提供的是支撑的维度——价格在什么位置能撑住、下跌时能跌多深，由供给决定；而价格能涨多高，更多由需求侧的叙事决定。 铜价之所以能维持在如此高的水平，与半导体、AI需求的叙事密切相关。 所以，很多宏观基金在配置上游电力相关资产时，会同时配置铜、核电所需的铀，以及燃气轮机等标的。这些配置的逻辑本质上是一样的，都是在押注AI资本支出的叙事。而从2026年6月到10月，我们一直在提示：从自由现金流开始转弱，到现在资本支出叙事的暂停乃至担忧，这一变化在10月份之后已经相当明显。 从持仓数据看，COMEX铜的投机性多头大部分来自宏观基金，它们持有多头是出于配置需求，并不是真的需要铜——真正需要铜的买家会体现在商业多头上。10月2日之后，这部分配置性需求开始大幅减弱，在10月2日至7日这一周的窗口里，宏观基金再次开始大规模减仓。背后的环境是：10年期美债收益率升至5%以上，AI资本支出叙事开始坍塌，美股的第二波下跌开始，费城半导体指数的第二波下跌也在加速，债务风险进一步蔓延。 这些因素叠加，导致基于AI资本支出叙事的配置开始大幅收缩...... 《付鹏说》第七季 已经正式上线， 大家点击订阅加入 。第七季我们也做出了全新的更新，权益的升级。付鹏说第七季一共包括五大主要的模块，分别是视频专栏、专属社群、深度文章、图表解答以及专属的问答。已经购买参加付鹏说第七季的小伙伴，大家不要忘记扫码图中的二维码，找到我们的客服小助手领取专栏资料。 付鹏说第七季 ，期待大家的加入。

articles.title: 高盛2027年中国股市展望：AI交易面临盈利压力，资金转向港股，MSCI中国指数有望涨23%
articles.summary: 11月16日，高盛最新发布的2027年中国市场策略展望报告 将港股评级上调至超配，同时下调A股至中性 ，核心逻辑在于：AI硬科技股盈利增速将显著放缓，A股估值面临一致预期下修压力，而港股正从估值低谷和互联网盈利拐点中获得支撑。 据追风交易台消息，该行设定2027年底MSCI中国指数目标价对应23%涨幅，沪深300目标点位4500点对应10%涨幅。Kinger Lau等分析师在报告中写道：当前MSCI中国指数12个月远期市盈率仅9.8倍，处于十年均值下方约1个标准差， "大量负面因素已经反映在股价中" 。 报告认为，2027年的核心交易逻辑已发生结构性转变——从押注AI贝塔行情，转向寻求盈利增长、现金回报和分散配置。分析师表示，A股在此前AI行情中积累的高仓位集中度，将成为制约指数上行的主要阻力。 盈利展望：港股加速，A股承压 该行预测2027年MSCI中国指数盈利增速为15%，沪深300指数为12%，均低于卖方一致预期的18%，但高于高盛对中期（5年）和长期（10年）每股盈利趋势增速（分别为10%和8%）的预测。 分市场来看，港股盈利将呈现超趋势增长。 分析师指出，这主要受互联网板块及更广泛软科技（Soft Tech）板块驱动——互联网板块盈利增速预计从2026年的-3%加速至2027年的18%，软科技从14%加速至22%，主要催化剂包括外卖补贴亏损的逐步消退（自2025年三季度以来累计亏损已达1900亿元人民币）以及AI/云收入的稳健增长。 A股则面临较大下修压力。 分析师团队指出， AI硬科技股盈利增速将从2026年的85%大幅放缓至2027年的46% ，而该板块目前占沪深300指数盈利权重的40%。高盛强调，A股市场卖方一致预期过于乐观是"A股市场的惯性特征"，实际盈利增速已连续7年低于预期。 在各板块具体预测中，该行对互联网、银行及"老消费"板块维持相对乐观，预计后两者将在净息差和投入成本温和改善的背景下延续稳健的盈利与现金流增长。与此同时，该行预测能源板块盈利将同比下滑，对汽车和科技硬件的预测亦较卖方一致预期偏保守。 AH股估值：降至低点，修复空间可期 该行认为，当前估值水平已提供较为充足的安全边际。 分析师指出，MSCI中国指数和沪深300指数目前分别以9.8倍和11.9倍12个月远期市盈率交易，前者处于十年均值下方约1个标准差，接近2024年9月初的周期低点。 历史经验显示，当MSCI中国以低于10倍的远期市盈率交易时，未来12个月产生正回报的概率超过85%，平均涨幅（以市值加权和中位数市盈率计算）分别约为14%和7%。 从国际比较角度，MSCI中国指数目前相对发达市场和除韩国以外的新兴市场分别折价43%和21%，PEG比率（市盈率相对盈利增长比率）在全球范围内具有吸引力。 高盛的宏观市盈率模型显示，考虑流动性和市场集中度因素后，MSCI中国指数的均衡远期市盈率应在11.5倍左右， 沪深300指数应在13.0倍左右，对应显著的估值修复空间。 资金流向：港股获机构青睐，A股仓位集中存隐忧 该行分析了各类投资者群体的配置动向，整体判断2027年中国股票的流动性背景将"大体上具有建设性"。 对冲基金 方面，据高盛Prime经纪数据，对冲基金目前对中国股票维持高总仓位但净仓位偏低，风险限额偏紧，该行预计其2027年将扩大在离岸市场的AI及非AI配置。 主动型长线基金 方面，离岸投资者对中国的配置已升至多年高位，但主要源于中国在基准指数中中性权重下降带来的被动超配，真正的主动加仓仍较有限。国内公募基金对AI硬科技仍保持重仓，该行预计其资金流向将向非AI板块倾斜。 南向资金 方面，该行预测2027年南向资金流入将达1000亿美元，高于年初至今的530亿美元。国内保险公司预计将在强劲保费增长的支撑下小幅增加股票配置，但其股票仓位已达投资组合的15%至16%，上行空间有限。 国家队 方面，该行估算国家队在2026年下半年已净买入约700亿美元A股（此前上半年为净卖出约3000亿美元）。 股票供给 方面，该行预计2027年IPO及配股融资规模将从2026年约2700亿美元的高位有所回落，而企业现金回报（包括股息和回购）预计将再创历史新高，达约4.1万亿元人民币（约合6300亿美元），足以抵消潜在的新增供给压力。 市场策略：港股超配，A股聚焦阿尔法 该行明确将港股上调至区域超配，同时将A股从超配下调至中性， 并建议A股投资者"以阿尔法取代贝塔"。 报告指出，自高盛于2026年6月3日将H股调整至中性以来，MSCI中国指数已下跌12%，落后全球发达市场12个百分点。如今，H股评级重新上调至超配，时机选择上兼顾了估值修复潜力和港股指数相对于A股指数更高的软科技（AI应用层）暴露度。 相比之下，A股面临的制约更加明显。该行指出， A股的三重压力在于：卖方一致预期的盈利增速（18%）显著高于高盛预测（12%）；AI硬科技盈利增速将大幅放缓；国内机构在AI硬科技方向的仓位仍高度集中。 该行的A/H市场轮动框架亦显示，未来3个月港股相对A股的表现将更具优势。 该行围绕中国成长股构建了三条核心主题投资方向： 其一，精选结构性AI成长标的 。当前AI代理股的大幅回调提供了较具吸引力的战略建仓机会，重点布局方向包括中国AI国内冠军企业（Domestic Champions）、AI出口领军企业（Export Leaders）及精选AI综合组合（Select AI Portfolio），后者自2024年初以来已累计上涨76%。 其二，稳定股东回报增长 。该行认为这一策略在美国利率高企、中国利率受压的环境中尤为有效。该行近期将银行股上调至超配，并持续看好股东回报主题。 其三，周期/消费成长中的盈利反转及自由现金流潜力标的 。该行指出，部分去评级（De-rated）和周期性成长（Cyclical Growth）板块的估值已跌至历史低位，盈利预期被压缩至保守水平， 互联网板块的盈利和自由现金流周期有望在未来几个季度触底回升。 articles.summary: 1—10月，我国高技术产业投资稳步提升，知识产权产品投资快速增长。 11月16日国家统计局发布数据，全国固定资产投资（不含农户）364824亿元，同比下降8.1%。其中，知识产权产品投资同比增长9.2%。 分领域看，基础设施投资同比下降5.1%，制造业投资下降2.9%，房地产开发投资下降21.6%。 高技术产业投资同比增长4.0%，其中信息服务业，航空、航天器及设备制造业，电子及通信设备制造业投资分别增长20.5%、10.2%、6.6%。 分产业看， 第一产业投资7018亿元，同比下降6.1%；第二产业投资142333亿元，下降3.6%；第三产业投资215473亿元，下降10.9%。 工业投资同比下降3.6%。其中，采矿业投资增长2.5%，制造业投资下降2.9%，电力、热力、燃气及水生产和供应业投资下降7.7%。 基础设施投资（口径详见附注1）同比下降5.1%。其中，信息传输业投资增长32.0%，航空运输业投资增长12.5%，水上运输业投资增长12.5%。 分地区看， 东部地区投资同比下降11.5%，中部地区投资下降12.9%，西部地区投资下降9.2%，东北地区投资下降25.9%。 分登记注册统计类别看，内资企业固定资产投资同比下降7.9%，港澳台投资企业固定资产投资下降8.4%，外商投资企业固定资产投资下降6.6%。 1—10月份，民间固定资产投资同比下降11.4%。从环比看，10月份固定资产投资（不含农户）下降2.93%。 风险提示及免责条款 市场有风险，投资需谨慎。本文不构成个人投资建议，也未考虑到个别用户特殊的投资目标、财务状况或需要。用户应考虑本文中的任何意见、观点或结论是否符合其特定状况。据此投资，责任自负。
